name: Kennel cough (bordetella)
description: Highly contagious respiratory infection common after boarding or dog parks. Usually self-limiting in 1–3 weeks.
recommended_actions: Rest and limit strenuous exercise
Keep away from other dogs
Provide fresh water and soft food if throat is sore
Monitor for worsening — vet visit if symptoms persist beyond 2 weeks or fever develops

suggested_tasks.title: Limit walk to short toilet break

name: Canine parvovirus
description: Life-threatening viral disease affecting unvaccinated or partially vaccinated dogs. Requires emergency veterinary care immediately.
recommended_actions: Go to an emergency vet immediately — this is life-threatening
Do not offer food or water without vet guidance
Isolate from other dogs completely
Bring vaccination records to the vet

name: Urinary tract infection (UTI)
description: Bacterial infection of the bladder or urethra. Common in female dogs and cats. Usually responds well to antibiotics.
recommended_actions: Schedule vet appointment within 24–48 hours for urine test and antibiotics
Encourage water intake
Extra toilet trips outside
Monitor for signs of kidney involvement — fever, back pain, lethargy

name: Ear infection (otitis externa)
description: Infection of the outer ear canal, often caused by yeast, bacteria, or ear mites. Very common in floppy-eared dogs.
recommended_actions: Schedule vet appointment for diagnosis and ear drops prescription
Do not insert anything into the ear canal
Gently clean outer visible area only
Keep ear dry — no swimming until resolved

name: Flea infestation
description: External parasite infestation. Can cause flea allergy dermatitis and anemia in severe cases. Requires treating pet AND environment.
recommended_actions: Apply vet-recommended flea treatment (spot-on, oral, or collar)
Wash all bedding in hot water
Vacuum carpets and furniture thoroughly
Treat all pets in the household
Treat home environment with spray if infestation is heavy

suggested_tasks.title: Check all other pets for fleas

name: Hyperthyroidism
description: Overactive thyroid gland — most common hormonal disorder in middle-aged and older cats. Very treatable with medication, diet, or radioiodine therapy.
recommended_actions: Schedule vet appointment for blood panel and thyroid level test
Note food and water intake changes to report to vet
Monitor weight weekly
Discuss medication vs dietary options with vet

suggested_tasks.title: Log daily food and water intake

name: Osteoarthritis
description: Chronic joint degeneration common in older or larger breed pets. Cannot be cured but is highly manageable with medication, weight management, and gentle exercise.
recommended_actions: Schedule vet appointment for assessment and pain management plan
Provide orthopedic bedding
Switch to low-impact short walks instead of long ones
Consider joint supplements (discuss with vet first)
Maintain healthy weight to reduce joint load

name: Dental disease
description: Periodontal disease affects most pets over age 3. Can lead to tooth loss and systemic infection if untreated. Preventable with regular brushing and dental cleanings.
recommended_actions: Schedule dental examination with vet
Start daily tooth brushing with pet-safe toothpaste
Offer dental chews as supplement (not replacement) to brushing
Consider professional dental cleaning under anesthesia

name: Anxiety / stress
description: Behavioral and physiological stress response. Common triggers include loud noises, separation, changes in routine, or new environments. Usually manageable with behavior modification and enrichment.
recommended_actions: Identify and reduce triggers where possible
Create a safe quiet space for the pet
Increase enrichment and interactive play
Consider pheromone diffuser (Adaptil/Feliway)
Consult vet if severe — medication or behavioral specialist may help

name: Obesity / overweight
description: Excess body weight significantly increases risk of diabetes, joint disease, heart disease, and cancer. Managed with portion control and increased activity.
recommended_actions: Weigh pet and compare to ideal breed weight
Measure all food portions precisely — stop free feeding
Replace high-calorie treats with vegetables (carrot, green bean for dogs)
Increase daily exercise gradually
Schedule vet check to rule out underlying thyroid or hormonal issues
